hypothesis: Non-financial HS300 firms whose year-over-year single-quarter revenue growth accelerates relative to the previous quarter should earn higher future returns than firms with decelerating revenue momentum.
selection_basis: R247 accounting quality had positive discovery and validation rank IC, but its executable quality composite failed validation, full-sample, recent-year and cost-stress gates. R248 changes the economic mechanism to demand momentum: it measures acceleration in seasonally comparable single-quarter revenue growth rather than absolute growth, profitability or accounting quality. The design was frozen after a no-forward-return coverage and correlation audit. Evidence: data/strategies/ai/.iterations/ai_hs300_multi_factor_rank/evidence/r248_data_feasibility.json

factor.formula: g_t - g_t_minus_1, where g_t = single_quarter_revenue_t / single_quarter_revenue_t_minus_4 - 1 and g_t_minus_1 = single_quarter_revenue_t_minus_1 / single_quarter_revenue_t_minus_5 - 1
factor.interpretation: Higher means the latest year-over-year single-quarter revenue growth is more positive than the immediately preceding quarter.
factor.pit_rule: Single-quarter revenue is derived from cumulative year-to-date reports. The effective date is the statutory reporting deadline plus 3 calendar days. The latest report expires after 500 calendar days.
factor.missing_data_rule: Require adjacent quarters t and t-1, their same-quarter observations one year earlier, and four positive revenue denominators. Missing components remain null; no partial score or zero fill.
factor.universe: historical HS300 membership excluding banks and non-bank financials using the current industry snapshot

strategies.weight_rationale: The revenue-acceleration score receives the same fixed 45% research weight used in R246 and R247. The remaining quality and cash weights preserve the 54.5/45.5 quality-cash ratio of the matched control. No weight was chosen using forward returns.
strategies.matched_requirements: Both strategies use the same non-financial HS300 universe, factor-availability filter, 30-name score limit, top 10 equal-weight positions, 20-day holding period, -20% stop loss, T+1 open execution, and cost model.

execution.cost_stress: 4x and 5x scale all four cost components proportionally

segments.stitching: compound two independently run segment curves; skip the first return of each later segment

factor_ic.method: month-end factor value versus T+1 open to T+21 open forward return within historical non-financial HS300 members; cross-sectional Spearman rank IC

gates.D1: full-period non-financial member-row factor coverage from 2023-01-03 onward >= 0.99
gates.D3: formula reconstruction and PIT audit pass; adjacent-quarter requirement and 500-day staleness are enforced
gates.D4: maximum mean absolute monthly rank correlation with the preregistered existing-factor set <= 0.70
gates.I1: discovery mean rank IC >= 0.02 with at least 18 month-end observations
gates.I2: validation mean rank IC >= 0.01 with at least 18 month-end observations and the same positive sign
gates.G2: discovery candidate MDD is no worse than control MDD by more than 5pp
gates.G4: full-sample candidate return > 0 and >= control return
gates.G5: full-sample candidate MDD <= 40% in absolute value and no worse than control by more than 5pp
gates.G6: rolling 1-year positive rate >= 60% and no worse than control by more than 2pp
gates.G7: recent 12-month candidate return > 0 and MDD no worse than control by more than 5pp
gates.G8: full-sample candidate return at 4x cost is positive
gates.G9: full-sample candidate return at 5x cost is positive
gates.C1: at least 30 distinct symbols are traded across the full sample
gates.C2: the largest symbol's share of net P&L is <= 25%
gates.C3: the top three symbols' share of net P&L is <= 55%
gates.C4: the top five symbols' share of net P&L is <= 75%
gates.C5: at least 8 distinct symbols have positive P&L in the validation segment
gates.C6: the largest industry's share of gross profit is <= 45%
gates.C7: the largest single-symbol loss is <= 20% of gross profit in absolute value

decision_rule: All D, I, G and C gates must pass. Any failure means the factor is not accepted and cannot be rescued by changing the formula, quarter window, weights, holding period, stop loss, universe, costs or gates after seeing results.
known_limitations: Single-quarter revenue is derived from cumulative year-to-date reports and may be noisy for firms with irregular fiscal calendars.
The factor uses accounting-report availability and can be stale between reports.
Financial values are current snapshots and may contain restatements.
The industry snapshot used to exclude financials is current rather than historical PIT.
Revenue acceleration can be cyclical and may select firms with temporarily depressed prior-year bases.
Passing these gates would justify further paper-trading validation, not production deployment.
